A_target.statement:
Let $M, N$ be $R$-[[Definition:Module|modules]] over a [[Definition:Commutative Ring with Unity|commutative ring]] $R$.
Then for every [[Definition:Bilinear Mapping|bilinear]] $\beta: M \times N \to P$ there is a [[Definition:Unique|unique]] linear $b: M \otimes_R N \to P$ with:
:$\map b {m \otimes n} = \map \beta {m, n}$

B_source.statement:
Let $F$ be the [[Definition:Free Module|free module]] on a set $S$ and $R' \subseteq F$ a [[Definition:Submodule|submodule]].
Then:
:$\map {\operatorname {Hom} } {F / R', P} \cong \set {f: S \to P: \text {the linear extension of } f \text { kills } R'}$

substitutions.the free object on a generating set: the free module on the set M x N
substitutions.the submodule of relations: the submodule generated by the bilinearity expressions
substitutions.the quotient by the relations: the tensor product M tensor N

derived.maps out of the quotient are maps killin: linear maps out of M tensor N are exactly bilinear maps on M x N
derived.the canonical map from generators into t: the bilinear map sending (m,n) to m tensor n

object_map.reformulation: Build the target as a quotient of a free object, so that its universal property becomes the statement that maps out of it kill the imposed relations.

validity_conditions: A module map out of a free module is uniquely determined by arbitrary values on the basis, here the set M x N.
Such a map kills the relation submodule precisely when the corresponding set map is bilinear, since the relations are exactly the bilinearity failures.
The universal property of the quotient then supplies existence and uniqueness of the induced map on M tensor N.
proof_plan: Form the [[Definition:Free Module|free module]] $F$ on the set $M \times N$, ignoring all structure on $M$ and $N$.

Let $R'$ be the submodule generated by the elements:
:$\tuple {m + m', n} - \tuple {m, n} - \tuple {m', n}$, $\tuple {m, n + n'} - \tuple {m, n} - \tuple {m, n'}$, $\tuple {r m, n} - r \tuple {m, n}$, $\tuple {m, r n} - r \tuple {m, n}$
and set $M \otimes_R N = F / R'$.
By the source result, linear maps $F / R' \to P$ correspond to maps $M \times N \to P$ whose linear extension kills $R'$, that is, [[Definition:Bilinear Mapping|bilinear maps]].

Hence $M \otimes_R N$ has the [[Definition:Universal Property|universal property]], with canonical bilinear map $\tuple {m, n} \mapsto m \otimes n$.
{{qed}}
